purpose: Auditable migration of maintainer instructions. This records preserved text and explicit resolution of stale Claude guidance; it does not claim agent compliance or runtime enforcement.

source.proseDisposition: Product identity and audience retained in AGENTS.md. Mandatory architecture reading replaced with explicit task-based routing while architecture remains authoritative.

rules.summary: Never require another person's approval to merge by default on any repository
Explain infrastructure changes by their practical benefit
For routine safeguards already declared in the project or authorized by the user, explain the benefit and proceed through spec/plan/apply
Make routine decisions instead of asking users to design infrastructure
When the application declares owner/contact settings, infer initial non-secret defaults from the repository's git identity and persist the reviewed values in its spec
For a new web project without an existing environment policy, prepare `production` and `staging` together under the application project and state the proposed setup directly
Surface cross-environment resource notes before claiming one environment validates another
Prefer HTTPS, private datastores, least-privilege workload identities, generated application secrets, managed CI deploys, and economical staging capacity wherever implemented
Default backup intent must cover every persistent database, declared or retained service mount, and object bucket through the shared provider contract
Hide provider setup complexity behind the desired-state lifecycle where possible
Ask only for missing access, genuinely ambiguous ownership or billing choices, external-party secrets, or consequential approvals required by the lifecycle contract
When a missing capability forces a user to perform routine provider setup manually, treat it as an onboarding product gap to fix in the shared application/provider path

Before implementing a provider-facing capability, define or extend the shared contract and check it against every named supported provider in the affected registry category, using official contracts/source
Treat existing code, comments, mocks, and previous agent conclusions as hypotheses, not independent proof of provider behavior
Follow `test/provider-contracts/README.md`
Check what the pinned schema actually constrains
For protobuf JSON responses, distinguish implicit scalar defaults from missing resource identity
Compare every affected interpretation across plan, apply, observation/status, and retry/recovery
Execute generated operational scripts in contract tests, including rejected and uncertain writes, operation/target correlation, terminal absence and secret-safe diagnostics
Complete the PR template's assumption/evidence/counterexample/test record, including observed failure before the fix and the passing result afterward
Keep regression tests in the ordinary `npm test` acceptance gate, not only an opt-in or scheduled suite
Keep known public endpoints separate from desired DNS management
Add the least code needed for the requested behavior
Keep MCP and CLI as thin adapters over `src/application`
Every supported command must be reachable through both adapters unless architecture documentation explicitly declares it interface-specific
Redact command results before they reach any interface

Credential handoffs must bind the approved origin and exact destinations, reject cross-origin redirects and request paths, bound response streaming through the body deadline, and render only validated value-free outcomes; an upstream error or receipt may echo the uploaded credential.
Cached credential expiry does not prove continuing authorization
Request externally owned credentials from the current plan's eligible input requirements, not every declared secret
The `hypervibe` CLI is safe to use because it shares Hypervibe state and reconciliation
rules.policyChange: Permit explicitly authorized operator-managed Railway private SSH diagnostics only; no automated provider CLI dependency, public TCP proxy creation, implicit key registration or infrastructure/data mutation. Preserve recorded-access cleanup and secret output boundaries.

rules.summary: Keep the desired-state loop central: `hv_spec` defines intent, `hv_plan` computes drift and blocked work, `hv_apply` converges a specific plan, and `hv_status` verifies convergence.
Lifecycle infrastructure changes belong in spec/plan/apply
Treat the persisted plan as an authorization boundary
A noop action must cause zero provider mutations
Treat observation as present/absent/unknown
Hosted observation must verify exact source provenance and independently authorized provider scope
Test first deployment with no local environment row as well as existing and partially bound environments
Resolve resource identity by durable provider id first
Keep resource naming in the shared deterministic naming policy
Treat naming changes as lifecycle changes, not cosmetic string edits

A cross-provider naming change is incomplete until tests cover the affected native namespaces, two environments with the same logical names, normalization/truncation collisions, preserved legacy bindings, and mutation-free noop
When a provider resource id is scoped by project, account, region, or environment, preserve the provider-native id and present its scope beside it in bindings, observations, and human output
When a new prerequisite rejects legacy metadata, provide a reviewed, preservation-safe normalization path where independent observation can prove the missing identity

On request-scaled platforms, background workers must explicitly receive continuous/instance CPU and a nonzero runtime floor; web services must explicitly preserve request-based CPU when the provider requires a value
Treat health probes as per-service runtime configuration
Release commands must run from the exact candidate image with its reviewed runtime configuration before any runtime workload changes

Any reviewed plan that asks a provider to build from a mutable branch must freeze the full source commit first and require provider-resolved provenance to match it before creating or updating release resources
Preserve a live workload's provider-observed runtime identity on updates

Treat provider-generated, non-retrievable credentials as a write-only transaction: validate the exact creation identity, verify all consumers before storing, persist the complete connection set atomically, and best-effort delete the exact new credential on every intervening failure
Generate passwords, tokens, and other secret material only with a cryptographically secure random source; `Math.random()` is never an acceptable secret generator.
Select deployment credentials with the exact repository scope
Generated CI may build an application image and update or execute exact provider resources that a reviewed apply already created and bound
For auto-deploy workflows, a first push with no applied desired-state marker must end as a neutral no-deploy bootstrap
Keep application workload kind separate from provider resource type
For scheduled workloads that require an initial CI release, separate untriggered resource preparation from reviewed trigger activation
Reusing a control-plane connection never establishes authority to copy its credential into application runtime
Keep environment-owned CI credentials and database URLs in the CI provider's exact environment scope

For existing-project CI savings, follow the project template's [adoption guide](https://github.com/davejohnson/project-template/blob/main/docs/ci-efficiency.md) and [testing skill](https://github.com/davejohnson/project-template/blob/main/.agents/skills/project-template-testing/SKILL.md)
Evaluate CI conditions only where their required context exists
Treat a managed GitHub Actions workflow's reviewed content hash plus semantic input hash as its lock
Require a managed GitHub Actions deploy branch to equal the provider-observed repository default branch
Treat a project-level generated CI program as one shared multi-environment contract
Make creates and destroys retry-safe and honest
Order multi-resource destroys by dependency and stop on unknown or failed deletion

Require lifecycle contract tests for noop mutation freedom, action-scoped mutation authority, observation errors, duplicate identities, import round trips, billable/data-bearing confirmation, and idempotent deletion
A storage provider id is supported only with a registered adapter covering private creation, ownership-safe observation, runtime wiring, streaming list/get/put, and confirmed teardown
Storage placement belongs in desired state, not connection credentials

Cloud storage must accept the provider-native local credential path (AWS default profile/SSO chain, Google Application Default Credentials, and the Azure default credential chain) as well as explicit automation credentials
Keep provider behavior behind the provider boundary
Generic commands such as `hv_inspect` and `hv_import` must not default to, narrow their schema to, expose identifier fields for, or dispatch directly to one provider
Report honestly
Before replacing a release-evidence format, preserve a read-only way to inspect an existing recovery baseline
Read-only inspection must not adopt repository edits, bootstrap legacy desired state, or write local environment files
Run-to-completion markers must be standalone provider log entries; caller-controlled values echoed in ordinary output cannot prove an exit
Treat provider support as an evidence ladder

Carry every declarative provider field through validation, observation, fingerprints, drift, action stale checks, create/update requests, receipts, and durable state; partial field support is not reconciliation.
Work stage-by-stage
Use `hv_inspect` for read-only provider forensics
Secrets never cross output boundaries
Deployment declarations describe managed resources, not every service an application uses
For one-time external handoffs, persist intent before consuming, retain received values encrypted until the local destination is committed, and reconcile a completed write whose receipt failed
Never ask a user to invent an opaque application secret that Hypervibe can generate safely
Provider errors can echo request inputs
Provider delivery diagnostics must keep connection-selection context separate from message provenance
Redacting a failed provider observation must preserve a closed, locally classified failure category and observation stage through orchestration receipts and their final alert consumer
Stale-plan fingerprints must include both environment-variable hashes and sorted key presence
Consequential confirmation is part of mutation authority, not a caller-only flag
Prefer `credentialsRef` with exported environment variables, `dotenv:` references, local JSON files, or secret-manager refs when asking users for credentials

Generated dotenv placeholders must be commented, idempotent, value-free, and receipt-bearing: never overwrite an existing value, never write before proving each exact private env path is untracked and repository-ignored, never make an ignored template trackable until every assignment is proven empty, reject symlinks and special files, remove group/world access without adding owner permissions, treat blanks as missing, and never copy provider credentials into runtime or environment-specific deploy files
Provider-declared local credential inputs must have one opinionated env slot per credential role, and every such slot must be classified as control-plane-only by the deploy-env boundary

Before writing repo-backed desired state or derived files, prove the current checkout belongs to the selected project using its committed spec or normalized repository identity; a spec-less unrelated checkout is not an empty canvas
Token and permission guidance must include the exact credential type, official creation URL, required permissions/scopes, resource scope, caveats, and a safe `hv_connections` example.

For an application's SendGrid sending key, give the [exact runtime-key instructions](docs/email-sender-readiness.md#application-sending-key-permissions): Restricted/Custom Access, Mail Send > Mail Send > Full Access (`mail.send`), and every other permission No Access
Whenever a GitHub PAT is required, provide a role-specific pre-filled creation URL with its name/description and required scopes or fine-grained permissions already selected
A successful administrative database query does not validate a workload's connection URL
When a provider rotates a canonical database password, bootstrap its dependent credential aliases and connection URLs using supported references rather than copied password literals
Repair existing credential aliases through an exact database action with raw-reference and resolved-value readback
Provider setup connections are never implicit application runtime secrets
Whenever a provider officially documents credential-template URLs, use them with the known required name and least-privilege permissions pre-filled
For push deploys, `deploy.trigger: "ci"` is the portable default
Dispatch Hypervibe-managed CI deploys only through `hv_ci_trigger`
Automated repair must fail closed when its declared failure evidence is absent or incomplete
Do not use temporary release-command changes for one-off data operations
Before a backup mutation, persist its exact scoped source and unique operation identity
Recurring recovery programs require exact published source/destination identities and a pinned helper artifact
Bind prior restore proof to native revisions captured from checksum-verified retained bytes
Admit provider combinations through shared capability metadata, not the independent existence of two adapters
Define persisted safety evidence with one runtime schema and derive its type from that schema
Cross-cutting deployment gates must preserve reviewed prerequisite stages without admitting workload or data writes
Dependency edges must represent actual prerequisites
Classify prerequisite failures separately from missing connections at their source
Portable execution authority must compare its source against a current, strict non-secret binding export
Do not introduce dependencies on provider CLIs for infrastructure operations
rules.policyChange: Permit explicitly authorized operator-managed Railway private SSH diagnostics only; no automated provider CLI dependency, public TCP proxy creation, implicit key registration or infrastructure/data mutation. Preserve recorded-access cleanup and secret output boundaries.

rules.summary: Do not run Hypervibe's full release gate, bump a version, or publish a release for every small change or merged pull request
A successful dependency install does not establish a clean security audit
When a release requires a separately deployed helper artifact, gate package publication on building, testing and verifying that exact helper
When building or releasing Hypervibe, update the configured local MCP runtime first and verify that it reports the new version
On macOS, configure every parent write descriptor used for child-process IPC with `F_SETNOSIGPIPE` before handing it to an async transport
Release macOS advisory instance locks explicitly with `flock(LOCK_UN)` before closing their descriptor
After creating a pull request, always provide its URL and explicitly offer to open it in the user's browser
When the complete, nonempty pull-request diff is limited to Hypervibe specs or files generated from them, prefix the title with exactly `[hypervibe] `
A shared container image default is distinct from each workload's runtime command
Generated-workflow tests must execute the emitted shell and JavaScript against a realistic multi-service fixture
Keep workflow-source provenance separate from deployed-source identity
Version release evidence and operational receipts from their shared validators and migrate every producer, generated consumer, runtime consumer, and fixture together
The managed iOS runtime (`templates/ios/hypervibe-ios-release.mjs`) must validate server evidence before provider effects and must never reuse an existing Apple build solely by version/build number
The managed iOS runtime owns build-number selection from a complete paginated App Store build listing; unknown, malformed, unsafe, or exhausted evidence must block rather than guess
Keep generated iOS `run` scripts within GitHub's 21,000-character limit
Distinguish failed execution from work that was never attempted

sections.heading: Behavioral Guidelines
sections.reason: Retain narrow scope, stated assumptions, concrete verification, and minimal changes. Clarification remains proportional to material ambiguity.

sections.heading: Think Before Coding
sections.reason: Preserve explicit uncertainty and evidence; current user-authorized routine choices do not require a redundant stop.

sections.heading: Simplicity First
sections.reason: Preserve minimal changes and no speculative layers; numeric line-count examples were illustrative, not an implementation contract.

sections.heading: Surgical Changes
sections.reason: Preserve unrelated work and trace changes to the requested outcome.

sections.heading: Goal-Driven Execution
sections.reason: Preserve concrete success criteria and observed failure/passing evidence.

sections.heading: Design Principles
sections.reason: Use the current desired-state, exact identity, redaction, and authorization contracts.

sections.heading: Let LLMs Handle Fuzzy Matching
sections.reason: Semantic interpretation may propose mappings; it cannot prove resource identity, scope, ownership, permissions, or adoption authority. Never return unredacted raw provider data.

sections.heading: Simple Shortcuts Are OK
sections.reason: Name interpretation is a proposal, not authority; durable scoped provider identity and ambiguity rules govern execution.

sections.heading: Two-Step Import Flow
sections.reason: Keep explicit read-only inspection, proposed exact mapping, and confirmed adoption; hv_import is not a generic read tool.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.reason: Replace stale src/tools/respond.ts and server ToolContext wiring with the command registry/context/results model. ToolContext remains a compatibility alias, not the active architecture.

sections.heading: The spec → plan → apply loop
sections.reason: Keep the desired-state loop; replace broad no-approval/local-fallback wording with exact action confirmation and unknown-observation rules.

sections.heading: Reconciliation safety
sections.reason: Preserved by the exact original AGENTS lifecycle rules and architecture contract.

sections.heading: Platform Bindings
sections.reason: Use the complete current durable binding contract rather than an incomplete example shape.

sections.heading: Environment Variables: Local Dev Exceptions
sections.reason: The application-specific reCAPTCHA bypass and recaptcha_sync advice has no corresponding current Hypervibe command. Runtime configuration follows the current generic declared-env contract; no application validation bypass is introduced.

additions.reason: User-requested direct forms with every supported known non-secret field prefilled; preserve contextual tool URLs across clients.
User-requested direct forms with every supported known non-secret field prefilled; preserve contextual tool URLs across clients.

postMigrationAdditions.reason: Preserve the owner-approved 2026-10-25 create-exclusive-v1 exception when integrating the maintainer guidance migration; existing DG-039 remains unchanged.

User-requested autonomous setup: an explicit bounded read-only continuation may recover pending identities without renewed approval. Dependent mutations, unknown-write replay, changed consequential actions and blocked/failed results retain their existing boundaries.
